title: The Rich Fool and the Nature of His Loss
english: Here, he has [wealth] in opposition to what his father had—the one who gathered wealth through toil—and his mother, who bequeathed him a possession. He will turn back to go as he has come, and he will take nothing of his toil. The fact of the history is clear: he takes nothing of what he labored for. He lets them go and did not know at the time, even if they come upon his enemies. 'He stores up,' he says, 'and does not know for whom he gathers them' (Luke 12:20). And the matter of the upward leading has been said already, that he does not take away anything of what his father and his mother, according to wickedness, make wealthy. Therefore, a praiseworthy mother may also be taken; here she has come to godliness, so that she may possess... [text illegible] ...to enjoy... and indeed this is an evil sickness; for just as it came to be, so it will depart. — Thus it is necessary to take [meaning]: if the entering into a place signifies a local entrance, so also the exiting. For I do not say that the one who entered this city left wickedness behind, but rather he entered here from another land or city. And what is his abundance, for which he toils toward the wind? His toil becomes wind, that is, his wealth is being overturned by nature; it is not becoming his own, not being held, so as even to be sent to a son. And indeed all his days are in darkness and in mourning. Darkness here means ignorance and the lack of clarity of things. And he mourns, missing those things which he hoped for, from which he thinks he has a pleasant life. And something stands before him. For mourning is raised up over death. In a certain way, therefore, he has died while living, 'and all his days are in darkness and he mourns' (Luke 12:21). And 'she who squanders,' he says, 'though living, has died' (1 Tim 5:6). If she has died, she is not worthy of being mourned; no mourning need be raised over her. For she lives only an empty life, but has died, having cast away the saving life, the blessed life — as though she had never squandered it, living after a merely human [fashion].
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
